title: Prophet Nuh and the Ark
summary: The story of Prophet Nuh 'alaihis salam, who built an ark by Allah's command and carried a pair of every kind of animal. (QS. Hud: 36-48; QS. Al-'Ankabut: 14)
moral: Trust in Allah's command, be patient in calling to good, and seek refuge with Him. Allah saves those who believe.
pages: Prophet Nuh 'alaihis salam called his people to Allah for nearly a thousand years. He invited them to worship Allah alone, but most of them refused and mocked him. Then Allah commanded him to build an ark.
Allah also commanded, 'Carry into the ark a pair of every kind.' (QS. Hud: 40). So the animals came in pairs, crowding in: rabbits, mouse deer, elephants, and birds.
When Allah's command came, the sky grew dark and rain poured down heavily. Water also gushed up from the earth. Prophet Nuh and the believers were already inside the ark with the pairs of animals.
The ark sailed on waves as high as mountains. Yet the ark stayed safe, for it was under Allah's protection. Not everyone was willing to board the ark, and those who refused were not saved.

Prophet Nuh said, 'Board it, in the name of Allah, whether it sails or anchors.' (QS. Hud: 41). Inside the ark everyone felt calm. The mouse deer, the rabbits, and the birds were at peace on the deck.
Then Allah said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, stop.' The water receded, the matter was finished, and the ark anchored on Mount Judi. The sun shone brightly again.

Prophet Nuh and his followers came down safely, and the animals returned to the earth. This story teaches us to be patient in doing good, to obey Allah, and to believe that His help will surely come. The end.
